short: Queen Mary I orchestrated the systematic execution of nearly three hundred Protestants.
full:
Beginning in January 1555, Queen Mary I's government launched a systemic and violent state campaign to eradicate Protestantism and formally restore Roman Catholicism in England. Enforcing newly revived medieval heresy laws, the Marian state rigorously tried and executed 284 obstinate reformers, burning most of them alive at the stake, including prominent leading figures like Thomas Cranmer, Hugh Latimer, and Nicholas Ridley.

The harsh persecutions largely failed to break the underground Protestant movement and instead dramatically galvanized deep anti-Catholic sentiment across the realm. Chronicled extensively and sensationally in John Foxe's immensely popular 'Book of Martyrs', the grim burnings deeply scarred the national consciousness, inextricably linking Catholicism with cruelty and foreign tyranny in the minds of the English public.
